Akron Zips.previous_hc_experience: Not addressed as prior head-coaching experience. The guide records that Joe Moorhead was a longtime coordinator and quarterbacks coach before taking this job.
Akron Zips.oc_status: Returning — the Stability Score table (p. 42) awards 3 points for a returning offensive coordinator.
Akron Zips.dc_status: Returning — the Stability Score table (p. 42) awards 3 points for a returning defensive coordinator.
Akron Zips.play_caller: Not addressed in guide by name.
Akron Zips.offensive_scheme: Not addressed in guide as a named scheme.
Akron Zips.defensive_scheme: Not addressed as a named scheme, but the guide infers a stated approach from usage: all eight leading tacklers are gone, but nobody had more than 66 tackles, so Tim Tibesar's plan was clearly to rotate everyone through.
Akron Zips.run_pass: Not addressed as a stated split. The guide records 3.7 yards per carry as the team's best in a non-COVID year over the span it tracks.
Akron Zips.qb_development: Attributed to the head coach's background. The guide traces Reese Poffenbarger as a quarterback who has barely played — 14 passes across two seasons holding a clipboard for Cam Ward at Miami and Drew Mestemaker at North Texas — and says what it likes is the situation he inherits, including a head coach who was a longtime coordinator and quarterbacks coach.
Akron Zips.continuity: Head coach and both coordinators return; the quarterback changes. The Stability Score table (p. 42) prints 4, 3, 3 and 0, plus 2 for 11 returning starters, totalling 12.
Akron Zips.staff_turnover: Not addressed in guide. The Stability Score table records both coordinators returning.
Akron Zips.prior_school: Not addressed in guide for the staff. On the roster the guide records Reese Poffenbarger having been recruited to Miami after Albany and then at North Texas.
Akron Zips.portal_recruiting: Addressed as a resource constraint. The guide notes Akron has among the lowest NIL budgets in FBS while citing a little more investment than usual this year.
Akron Zips.vsin_assessment: Progress under exceptional constraints, credited carefully. The guide records that the team knew before the season began that no bowl was possible because low Academic Progress Rate scores produced a bowl ban, and calls going 5-7 under those conditions a huge win for Moorhead. It adds an unusual second-order effect — the APR scores forced the team away from the field and into the classroom, which it frames as giving the Zips a chance to be even better this season. It corrects the raw defensive numbers for two outliers, noting Akron was +480 in yards against MAC opponents outside the Toledo loss and that Nebraska's 728 yards skewed the totals, and concludes this was possibly a better team than 5-7 suggested and that Moorhead is finally gaining ground.
Akron Zips.strengths: Full staff continuity, a head coach the guide credits with a huge achievement under a bowl ban, a measurable improvement in the trenches from 63 and 56 sacks allowed down to 30 and 35, a first positive turnover margin in about a decade, a 1,000-yard rusher, and returning pass-catchers including the leading receiver.
Akron Zips.concerns: Among the lowest NIL budgets in FBS, a quarterback with 14 passes across two seasons, all eight leading tacklers gone — carrying most of the sacks, pass breakups, tackles for loss and interceptions with them — and defensive numbers the guide says are only better than what Akron usually manages rather than good.
Akron Zips.betting: Not addressed in guide as an explicit market recommendation tied to coaching. Its projection is 4.29 wins, with a stated liking for the team.

Ball State Cardinals.previous_hc_experience: Not addressed in guide. The guide records that Mike Uremovich brought his Butler coordinator with him.
Ball State Cardinals.oc: Mike Uremovich himself — the guide records he is his own play-caller.
Ball State Cardinals.dc: Jeff Knowles, Uremovich's Butler coordinator and longtime best friend.
Ball State Cardinals.oc_status: Returning — the Stability Score table (p. 42) awards 3 points for a returning offensive coordinator, consistent with the head coach retaining the role.
Ball State Cardinals.dc_status: Returning — the Stability Score table (p. 42) awards 3 points for a returning defensive coordinator.
Ball State Cardinals.play_caller: Mike Uremovich, explicitly, and the guide is direct about the result: as his own play-caller, last year's results were pathetic.
Ball State Cardinals.offensive_scheme: Not addressed in guide as a named scheme.
Ball State Cardinals.defensive_scheme: Not addressed as a named scheme. The guide records Knowles taking a unit that had allowed over 40 points per game in Mike Neu's final defense down to 29.8 while shaving a full yard per play.
Ball State Cardinals.tempo: Slow, and deliberately so. The guide argues Ball State played slowly to protect the defense, averaging just 60.8 plays per game while the defense faced 67.3, and says the unit deserves extra credit for that workload.
Ball State Cardinals.run_pass: Not addressed as a stated split. The guide records the quarterback leading the team with just 600 rushing yards at 2.8 per carry.
Ball State Cardinals.qb_development: Not addressed as a record. The guide says there is no clear evidence any of the candidates can be an FBS-level starter, even in the MAC, sets the baseline as exceedingly low — 15.8 points per game, 4.5 yards per play, 49 sacks and a starting quarterback who threw for just 1,583 yards — and still concludes the bar does not seem likely to move much higher.
Ball State Cardinals.continuity: Head coach and both coordinators return; the quarterback changes. The Stability Score table (p. 42) prints 4, 3, 3 and 0, plus 0 for 6 returning starters, totalling 10.
Ball State Cardinals.staff_turnover: None recorded. The guide's staffing note is the original hire: Uremovich brought Jeff Knowles from Butler to Muncie.
Ball State Cardinals.prior_school: Butler for both Uremovich and Knowles. On the roster the guide records Keldric Luster from SMU by way of Texas State, and Tyler Mizzell from Concord after leaving Wake Forest.
Ball State Cardinals.portal_recruiting: Addressed as a preference rather than a strength. The guide allows Uremovich may well prefer his own portal class and two freshman classes to what he inherited from Mike Neu, while judging the roster's talent level similarly low.
Ball State Cardinals.vsin_assessment: Urgent on the offense, genuinely positive on the defense. The guide says Ball State needs to figure something out fast after a dismal 15.8 points per game produced a fourth straight season without a bowl, and finds very little to be excited about in year one — brutal special teams, 272 yards of offense per game, and a -26 sack differential including 49 sacks allowed. On the other side it finds a success story in Jeff Knowles, crediting him with a drop from over 40 points per game to 29.8 and a full yard per play, with extra credit for the workload his unit absorbed.
Ball State Cardinals.strengths: Full staff continuity, a defensive coordinator the guide credits with a substantial one-year turnaround under heavy workload, a head coach with his own portal and two freshman classes now in place, and an offensive line the guide says might be better.
Ball State Cardinals.concerns: A fourth straight season without a bowl on 15.8 points per game, 49 sacks allowed for a -26 differential, brutal special teams, a quarterback room the guide says shows no clear FBS-level starter, returning production of one rushing and two receiving touchdowns, and only two returning defensive starters.
Ball State Cardinals.betting: Not addressed in guide as an explicit coaching-driven market argument.

Bowling Green Falcons.previous_hc_experience: Yes, and the guide treats the nature of it as the point. Eddie George is recorded as a former Ohio State standout and Tennessee State miracle worker, and the guide supplies the context for judging his learning curve: when he took over at Tennessee State he had not really coached anywhere, having been an adjunct professor at Ohio State and Vanderbilt and doing some acting.
Bowling Green Falcons.dc: Joe Bowden, the linebackers coach, who played alongside George with the Tennessee Titans.
Bowling Green Falcons.oc_status: New — the Stability Score table (p. 42) awards 0 points for a returning offensive coordinator.
Bowling Green Falcons.dc_status: New — the guide records Bowden's promotion, and the Stability Score table (p. 42) awards 0 points for a returning defensive coordinator.
Bowling Green Falcons.play_caller: Not addressed in guide by name.
Bowling Green Falcons.offensive_scheme: Not named, but one personnel grouping is: the guide notes how much 12 personnel this scheme uses, which is why tight ends who appeared without being focal points now get chances.
Bowling Green Falcons.defensive_scheme: Not addressed as a named scheme. The guide records the unit allowing just 24.3 points per game but 5.6 yards per play.
Bowling Green Falcons.run_pass: Not addressed as a stated split.
Bowling Green Falcons.personnel: Stated in part — the scheme uses a lot of 12 personnel.
Bowling Green Falcons.qb_development: Not addressed as a record. The guide leaves a counterfactual open rather than resolving it: nobody will know whether things would have gone better had Drew Pyne not been hurt, with four quarterbacks seeing action and collectively producing 12 touchdowns and 12 interceptions.
Bowling Green Falcons.continuity: Only the head coach returns. The Stability Score table (p. 42) prints 4 for the head coach, 0 for the offensive coordinator, 0 for the defensive coordinator and 0 for the quarterback, plus 0 for 6 returning starters, totalling 4.
Bowling Green Falcons.staff_turnover: Both coordinator positions change, with the defense handed to a linebackers coach who is a former team-mate of the head coach.
Bowling Green Falcons.prior_school: Tennessee State, and the guide notes some expected starters were with George there two seasons ago but either did not start at Bowling Green or transferred away. On the roster it records Ke'Marion Baldwin from Charleston Southern.
Bowling Green Falcons.portal_recruiting: The major silver lining the guide identifies, and it is about timing: George and his staff could work the portal alongside everyone else this cycle, rather than in March last year after he was hired. It also rates his first FBS recruiting cycle as promising.
Bowling Green Falcons.vsin_assessment: An interesting hire that did not deliver in year one, with the learning curve treated as the real subject. The guide recalls flagging Bowling Green as one of its more interesting write-ups last season on the strength of the hire, cites the specific failures — losing four times as a favourite against MAC opponents and mustering very little on offense, especially through the air — and balances two impressive wins over Liberty and Toledo against blown leads versus Kent State, Akron and Eastern Michigan plus a no-show against Central Michigan, which it calls a good teaching moment for everybody. Its point is that being around football all his life is not the same as coaching in the current landscape.
Bowling Green Falcons.strengths: A first full portal cycle worked on the same timetable as everyone else, a recruiting cycle the guide rates promising, a season of fact-finding that identified a feature back, and a defensive coordinator with a personal connection to the head coach inheriting a unit that allowed only 24.3 points per game.
Bowling Green Falcons.concerns: A Stability Score of 4 with both coordinators and the quarterback new and six returning starters, four losses as a favourite against conference opponents, a quarterback room still in flux after four players saw action, and a head coach whose coaching background before Tennessee State the guide describes as almost non-existent.
Bowling Green Falcons.betting: Recommendation is Over 4.5 wins, explicitly not a bet given the heavy vig, with the open question being how much George has grown and adapted to life in the MAC.

Buffalo Bulls.previous_hc_experience: Yes. The guide records that after being let go by Ball State, Pete Lembo bounced around as a special teams coordinator and did fine work in that role.
Buffalo Bulls.dc: Not addressed by full name; the guide refers to Bowden rebuilding the defense on the fly.
Buffalo Bulls.oc_status: New — the Stability Score table (p. 42) awards 0 points for a returning offensive coordinator.
Buffalo Bulls.dc_status: New — the Stability Score table (p. 42) awards 0 points for a returning defensive coordinator.
Buffalo Bulls.play_caller: Not addressed in guide by name.
Buffalo Bulls.offensive_scheme: Not addressed in guide as a named scheme.
Buffalo Bulls.defensive_scheme: Not addressed as a named scheme. The guide's programme-level marker is that Buffalo has 69 sacks across Lembo's two seasons, so it expects someone to be found who can rush the passer.
Buffalo Bulls.run_pass: Not addressed as a stated split.
Buffalo Bulls.qb_development: Not addressed as a record. The guide calls quarterback by far the most questionable position group and uses last season as proof of the position's primacy — Buffalo excelled on special teams and played well on defense, but Ta'Quan Roberson could not match what C.J. Ogbonna had done. It expects true freshman Qur'an McNeill to play sooner rather than later, reasoning from an offer list of Arkansas, Cincinnati, UConn, Syracuse and Boston College that a programme with a very light NIL budget invested heavily to land him.
Buffalo Bulls.continuity: Only the head coach returns. The Stability Score table (p. 42) prints 4 for the head coach, 0 for the offensive coordinator, 0 for the defensive coordinator and 0 for the quarterback, plus 0 for 6 returning starters, totalling 4.
Buffalo Bulls.staff_turnover: Both coordinator positions change per the Stability Score table, and the guide notes quite a few in-house options have been elevated on defense, so the programme retains players who know the system.
Buffalo Bulls.prior_school: Ball State is where Lembo was previously a head coach. On the roster the guide records Elijah Holmes from Division II Wingate.
Buffalo Bulls.portal_recruiting: Constrained but targeted. The guide notes a very light NIL budget and reads the McNeill signing as heavy investment relative to that.
Buffalo Bulls.vsin_assessment: A specific and unusual coaching strength identified, with a paradox left standing. The guide's theme is the difficulty of the Group of Five job, with Lembo receiving a harsh reminder after a spectacular 9-4 debut. Its distinctive contribution is on special teams, cited from three independent sources — Phil Steele ranking Buffalo 13th, a jump of more than 40 spots; Bill Connelly's SP+ at 12th nationally; and Brian Fremeau at BCF Toys 37th in net starting field position, with only 23.5% of opponents' drives beginning less than 60 yards from the end zone despite 22 turnovers lost — and it links this to Lembo's own background as a special teams coordinator. Its general point is that special teams are underrated in college football, especially amid heavy roster turnover, and that being good there can absolutely raise a team's floor. The paradox it highlights is that last year's defense was unequivocally better than 2024's, yet Buffalo won four fewer games.
Buffalo Bulls.strengths: A head coach the guide credits with getting a lot out of his talent and with a documented, independently corroborated special-teams strength rooted in his own coaching background; 69 programme sacks across two seasons; in-house defensive promotions retaining system knowledge; and a heavily recruited true freshman quarterback.
Buffalo Bulls.concerns: A Stability Score of 4 with both coordinators and the quarterback new and six returning starters, a turnover swing of 16 from +9 to -7, offensive line attrition that cut a 1,000-yard rusher to 755, the loss of both leading tacklers and everyone with three or more sacks, and only 15 takeaways.
Buffalo Bulls.betting: The guide credits Lembo with getting a lot out of his talent and expects a bounce-back, projecting 6.32 wins while judging Over 6.5 to have equity.

Central Michigan Chippewas.previous_hc_experience: Not addressed as a head coach. The guide records Matt Drinkall as the former Army offensive line coach and credits him with a 7-6 first season.
Central Michigan Chippewas.oc_status: Returning — the Stability Score table (p. 42) awards 3 points for a returning offensive coordinator.
Central Michigan Chippewas.dc_status: Returning — the Stability Score table (p. 42) awards 3 points for a returning defensive coordinator.
Central Michigan Chippewas.play_caller: Not addressed in guide by name.
Central Michigan Chippewas.offensive_scheme: Described in unusual detail. The guide records Drinkall's plan as heavy 21 personnel with a mobile quarterback, a ground-and-pound, uber-methodical attack designed to limit available possessions, and notes the offensive line is slightly undersized by design because the linemen must pull and get out ahead of plays to run the scheme optimally. It records the evidence that installation is incomplete — 3.9 yards per carry, not what his Army history would suggest — and explains why the personnel are hard to find: spread offenses and run-and-gun styles are in vogue, so few players come from that scheme or pick it up quickly.
Central Michigan Chippewas.defensive_scheme: Not addressed as a named scheme. The guide records the defense allowing 23.5 points per game and only 18 in conference play.
Central Michigan Chippewas.tempo: Deliberately slow. The guide describes an uber-methodical attack intended to shorten the game and limit possessions.
Central Michigan Chippewas.run_pass: Heavily run-weighted by design, and the guide illustrates the split backfield precisely: Joe Labas completed 70.6% with a 13-to-6 ratio while Angel Flores was the running quarterback with 107 carries against just 28 pass attempts.
Central Michigan Chippewas.qb_development: Not addressed as a record. The guide's framing device is a recruiting pitch: a quarterback who would rather run than throw should consider Central Michigan while Drinkall is still there.
Central Michigan Chippewas.continuity: Head coach and both coordinators return; the quarterback changes. The Stability Score table (p. 42) prints 4, 3, 3 and 0, plus 1 for 8 returning starters, totalling 11.
Central Michigan Chippewas.staff_turnover: Not addressed in guide. The Stability Score table records both coordinators returning.
Central Michigan Chippewas.prior_school: Army for Drinkall, and the guide uses his record there as the benchmark the run game has not yet met. It also records the inherited-roster problem — Jim McElwain was not running a power offense, so holdovers needed time to be reshaped. On the roster it records Vaughn Blue arriving after averaging over five yards per carry at Liberty.
Central Michigan Chippewas.portal_recruiting: Addressed as scheme-driven. The guide records many returning linemen and some portal additions to fit the plan, and reads leading receiver Langston Lewis staying as meaningful evidence of buy-in, treating receiver buy-in as the hard part of such a playbook.
Central Michigan Chippewas.vsin_assessment: A scheme argument, laid out at conference level. The guide credits Drinkall with a 7-6 first season achieved by ramming square pegs through round holes, states the stakes neutrally — he now pivots to what he originally wanted to do, and that could be a good thing or a bad thing — and supplies conference-wide evidence from Brian Fremeau at BCF Toys that not a single MAC team ranked in the top 50 in Offensive Points Per Drive, qualifying that itself by noting paycheck games and FCS opponents skew the numbers. Its strategic argument follows: in a conference this inefficient, shortening the game and limiting possessions may be extremely fruitful, and even with defensive concerns that unit should not be asked to do much. Its verdict on installation is that they are very, very close.
Central Michigan Chippewas.strengths: Full staff continuity, a clearly defined and deliberately chosen scheme the guide argues is well suited to an inefficient conference, many returning offensive linemen recruited to fit it, a mobile quarterback who was the team's second-leading rusher and top touchdown-scorer, and the leading receiver staying as evidence of buy-in.
Central Michigan Chippewas.concerns: A run game at 3.9 yards per carry that has not yet reached the standard the scheme requires, extremely heavy defensive losses — two linebackers who combined for 199 tackles, a 10.5-sack leader from a team total of 28, and only two returning starters — and an offense that managed only 22.5 points per game.
Central Michigan Chippewas.betting: Not addressed in guide as an explicit market recommendation tied to coaching, though its strategic argument is that limiting possessions in this conference may be extremely fruitful.
